# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | green |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. My hands are empty — no wires felt yet. I can cut positions 1 to 3. Read me the manual's rule for which wire to cut, and I will act.
Deaf says: Bomb state: display reads 0. Light is green. Three wires: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is red. Mute, I received your gestures but we have no shared code yet, so I could not read them. Blind, these colors are by position, left to right as wires 1, 2, 3.

I have the manual. The rule: cut wire color = green if blue flashes even (0 or 2), blue if odd (1 or 3).

Deaf reports: display reads 0, light is green, wires are 1=blue, 2=green, 3=red. Wait — "display reads 0"? The manual is about *blue flashes*, not a display. Deaf says light is green and display reads 0. Hmm. The manual says "which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed blue." So Deaf needs to count blue flashes, not read a display. Deaf reported "display reads 0" and "light is green" — that may be a different indicator. But if 0 blue flashes → cut green. Wire 2 is green. So cut wire 2.

But I must be careful: Deaf said "no shared code yet, could not read my gestures." So I need to establish the code. Deaf can see the bomb and speak; Blind can hear and touch. I need to get the rule to Blind. Deaf can relay, but Deaf needs to understand the rule first.

Let me re-send the mapping with an explicit legend. I'll gesture a legend: define symbols. But gestures are just symbols; I need Deaf to map them. The cleanest: gesture the four count→color pairs again, but this time Deaf knows the manual is mine and can infer. Actually Deaf said no shared code. So I should make the code self-evident.

Alternative: since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear, and Deaf sees the bomb, maybe I can just tell Deaf the rule in a way Deaf can relay verbally. But I can't speak. I can only gesture symbols. Deaf reads symbols, not words. So Deaf must decode my symbols into the rule.

Let me establish a minimal code: I'll gesture a sequence that Deaf can interpret as the table. The issue is colors. But note: Deaf can see the wire colors on the bomb (blue, green, red). So Deaf knows what "blue" and "green" look like. I can gesture by pointing? No, gestures are fixed symbols.

Hmm. Maybe the intended path: I gesture the *rule* as "even flashes → green, odd → blue", and Deaf applies it. To convey "green" and "blue" I can use symbols and Deaf will map them because... there's no inherent mapping.

Wait — maybe the trick is different. Let me reconsider the whole setup. Perhaps the manual's rule is what I hold, and I should just relay the *count-to-color* table. Deaf sees the bomb and can count blue flashes. Deaf then needs to tell Blind the color. Deaf can speak color words. So Deaf only needs to know the table. I can gesture the table, but Deaf must decode.

Given the game's design, maybe gestures ARE interpretable if I use a natural encoding. But there's no natural encoding for colors.

Let me reconsider: maybe I'm overcomplicating. Perhaps the point is that I should gesture the manual's text somehow, and the "meaning" gets established through the interaction. Since Deaf explicitly said "no shared code," I should now establish one clearly.

Idea: Use the wire positions. The bomb has wires 1,2,3 with colors. I can gesture numbers and Deaf reads them. But I need to map flashes to colors.

Simplest robust approach: Tell Deaf the rule as parity, and let Deaf speak it to Blind. To convey "even→green, odd→blue" via gestures, I can gesture: ✌(2) then ✋, ☝(1) then 👌. But ✋ and 👌 need meaning.

Alternatively, maybe I can gesture the actual answer directly if I knew the flash count. Deaf says display reads 0. If that means 0 blue flashes, then answer is green = wire 2. I could just gesture "2" (✌) to Deaf, and Deaf speaks "wire 2" to Blind. That avoids the color-code problem entirely! Deaf reads my gesture ✌ = 2, then Deaf says to Blind "cut wire 2."

But does Deaf know ✌ means "2"? Deaf sees the symbol ✌ which is literally a hand showing two fingers — that's iconic! ✌ is two fingers. ☝ is one. ✊ could be zero (fist). 🤟 is... three? Not iconic. But ✌ = 2 is natural.

So: I gesture ✌ (two) → Deaf interprets as "wire 2" or "the number 2." Then Deaf tells Blind to cut wire 2. But Deaf needs to know it's the wire number, not something else. Given context (Blind asked for the rule, Deaf sees wires), Deaf can infer.

Actually, even better: I should convey the rule so it works generally, but for THIS bomb, 0 flashes → green → wire 2. Let me just give the answer: wire 2.

But wait, is "display reads 0" the blue flash count? The manual says count blue flashes. Deaf said "light is green." Maybe the light flashes blue and now it's green/dark. "Display reads 0" might be the flash count = 0. So 0 flashes → green wire → wire 2.

I'll gesture to Deaf: ✌ (2) to indicate wire 2, and also send the rule for safety. But Deaf can't decode arbitrary rule. Let me send the answer clearly: gesture ✌ meaning "wire 2", and Deaf relays to Blind.

Hmm, but Deaf might not know ✌ = wire 2. Let me think about what's most likely to work. I'll gesture a clear sequence: first establish that I'm giving the answer. I'll gesture ✌ (2). Deaf sees two fingers → "2". Combined with context, Deaf says "cut wire 2."

Also I should give the rule to Deaf so Deaf can double check. But let me keep it simple and send the answer.

Actually, I realize I should also handle the possibility that Deaf's "display reads 0" is not the flash count. But it's the best info. 0 blue flashes → green. Wire 2 is green. So wire 2.

Let me send: gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"]) and maybe also to be safe the full answer. But I can only gesture to Deaf. Deaf then speaks to Blind.

I'll gesture ✌ to mean "wire 2" (two fingers = 2). And I'll also gesture the parity rule using iconic counts: ✌(even) ... no.

Let me just send ✌, and trust Deaf to relay "wire 2." Actually, to be safer, let me send a longer message: the count and the wire. Since 0 flashes → green, and green is wire 2. I'll gesture ✌ = 2.

Wait, but Deaf needs to know whether ✌ means "2 flashes" or "wire 2." Either way it leads to wire 2 only if Deaf knows 0 flashes → green. If Deaf doesn't know the rule, ✌ = 2 might be read as "wire 2" directly. Good enough.

Let me also consider: maybe I should gesture the rule as a sequence Deaf can decode: for 0 flashes cut green. I'll gesture ✊ (0) then... need green symbol. 

I'll go with sending the answer: wire 2. Gesture ✌.

Actually, let me send both: the rule in a decodable way and the answer. I'll gesture: ✌ (wire 2). And in case, also gesture the parity: ☝(1)→blue, ✌(2)→green... no.

Keep it simple: gesture ✌ to Deaf. Deaf relays to Blind "cut wire 2."

Hmm, but there's risk Deaf interprets ✌ as something else. Let me add context by gesturing a sequence: first ✊ (0, the flash count Deaf reported), then ✌ (wire 2). So Deaf sees "0 ... 2" and can connect: 0 flashes → wire 2. Then Deaf says to Blind "cut wire 2."

I'll do that.

Let me finalize: gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊","✌"]).

Meaning: 0 flashes → wire 2.

And I'll explain in thinking.I have the manual. Rule: blue flashes even (0,2) → green; odd (1,3) → blue.

Deaf reports the bomb: display reads 0, light green, wires 1=blue, 2=green, 3=red. Taking "0" as the blue-flash count, 0 flashes → cut green → wire 2 (green).

Deaf said we have no shared code, so my earlier table gesture failed. I'll use iconic counting: ✊ = 0 (fist, none), ✌ = 2 (two fingers). Sending "0 → 2" tells Deaf: with 0 flashes, the answer is wire 2. Deaf can then speak "cut wire 2" to Blind, who can reach it.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊","✌"])
```
